train_cfg.schedule_notes: Published DAROD schedule for CARRADA: 50 epochs, batch 4, Adam lr 1e-4 (paper Sec. 'Training setting'; colindecourt/darod config/config_carrada.json epochs/batch_size/lr). The scheduler there is ExponentialDecay(decay_rate=0.9, staircase=True, decay_steps=steps_per_epoch * scheduler_step) with scheduler_step=25, i.e. lr *= 0.9 every 25 epochs -- StepLR(step_size=25, gamma=0.9) here. NOT type 'exp': ExponentialLR decays every epoch, which after 50 epochs would leave lr at 0.9^50 = 0.5% of its initial value instead of 0.9^2 = 81%.
train_cfg.data_stats_notes: Standardization constants for the RD input, copied verbatim from the reference implementation colindecourt/darod, config/config_carrada.json (data_mean/data_std). Applied there in darod/utils/data_utils.py as (spectrum - data_mean) / data_std before the network sees it. Verified against this repo's CARRADA loader: measured mean 59.073 / std 3.747 over 11 batches of range_doppler_raw, against the reference's 58.471 / 3.749 -- our RD values were already on the reference's scale, only the standardization step was missing. These live in the TRAIN config rather than the model config because model_config is splatted into DAROD.__init__ (network.py:38), so every key there must be a constructor argument.
